title: Coi follow-up: ready to send
description: What Linda asked for first, ready on day one: “If I woke up tomorrow and there was a list of every policy renewing in the next 30 days that hasn't been quoted yet, soonest first, with a renewal email drafted to each client, I'd be thrilled.”
instructions:
Produce “Coi follow-up: ready to send” tonight — What Linda asked for first, ready on day one: “If I woke up tomorrow and there was a list of every policy renewing in the next 30 days that hasn't been quoted yet, soonest first, with a renewal email drafted to each client, I'd be thrilled.”.

Follow the procedure of the “Renewals due in 30 days” workflow, using only what is in the knowledge base and memory so far:
1. Pull the list of cois from Applied Epic: adjuster, what is open, value, and last contact.
2. Prioritize by value and age; skip anyone contacted in the last 7 days.
3. Draft one short, personal email per adjuster that names exactly what is open and makes the next step easy (book a time, send the document, reply yes).
4. Request approval from Linda before anything goes to an adjuster.
5. Schedule a second touch 4 days later for anyone who has not replied; stop after three touches and list them for a personal call.
6. Deliver the queue as one document: a table (adjuster, what is open, value, last contact, drafted message, next step) with the drafts below it; save replies and outcomes to memory.
7. Hard rules from the call, in every draft: “Never quote a premium or tell a client their coverage is bound. Only a licensed agent, me or Jamal, can do that.” “Never contact Castillo Builders about anything.”

You were hired for: Renewals due in 30 days. Show this first piece of work in the format those workflows will use.

Deliver it as one document. Label any assumption, and list exactly what you still need from the team.
